knowledge_point.title: Finding the Value of an Unknown Such That a Vector Lies in the Span of Given Vectors

question.:question/problem:
Find the value of $k$ such that $\mathbf{b}\in\operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2\}$, where

$$
\mathbf{a}_1=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\qquad\mathbf{a}_2=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -6 \\ -3\end{bmatrix},\qquad\mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ k \\ 18\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
By definition, $\mathbf{b}\in\operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2\}$ exactly when $x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2=\mathbf{b}$ has a solution. Equating coordinates gives

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}- 2 x_{1} + 3 x_{2} &=-14 \\ 4 x_{1} - 6 x_{2} &=k \\ 3 x_{1} - 3 x_{2} &=18\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Form the augmented matrix:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-2 & 3 & -14 \\ 4 & -6 & k \\ 3 & -3 & 18\end{array}\right]
$$

Place the two known-coordinate equations first (a row permutation).

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-2 & 3 & -14 \\ 3 & -3 & 18 \\ 4 & -6 & k\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_1\leftarrow \left(- \frac{1}{2}\right)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & - \frac{3}{2} & 7 \\ 3 & -3 & 18 \\ 4 & -6 & k\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_2\leftarrow R_2-(3)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & - \frac{3}{2} & 7 \\ 0 & \frac{3}{2} & -3 \\ 4 & -6 & k\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_3\leftarrow R_3-(4)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & - \frac{3}{2} & 7 \\ 0 & \frac{3}{2} & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & k - 28\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_2\leftarrow \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & - \frac{3}{2} & 7 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & k - 28\end{array}\right]
$$

The last row represents $0x_1+0x_2=k - 28$. Consistency therefore requires

$$
\begin{aligned}0 &=k - 28 \\ k &=28.\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot equations give $x_2=-2$ and $x_1=4$. These values also establish sufficiency:

$$
(4)\mathbf{a}_1+(-2)\mathbf{a}_2=\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ 28 \\ 18\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Therefore, $k=28$ is the only value for which the vector lies in the span.

knowledge_point.title: Finding the Value of an Unknown Such That a Vector Lies in the Span of Given Vectors

question.:question/problem:
Find the value of $k$ such that $\mathbf{b}\in\operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2\}$, where

$$
\mathbf{a}_1=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\qquad\mathbf{a}_2=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\qquad\mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix}6 \\ k \\ 3\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
By definition, $\mathbf{b}\in\operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2\}$ exactly when $x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2=\mathbf{b}$ has a solution. Equating coordinates gives

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}- x_{1} + x_{2} &=6 \\ - 3 x_{1} + 3 x_{2} &=k \\ x_{1} + 2 x_{2} &=3\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Form the augmented matrix:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-1 & 1 & 6 \\ -3 & 3 & k \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

Place the two known-coordinate equations first (a row permutation).

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-1 & 1 & 6 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ -3 & 3 & k\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_1\leftarrow (-1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -1 & -6 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ -3 & 3 & k\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_2\leftarrow R_2-(1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -1 & -6 \\ 0 & 3 & 9 \\ -3 & 3 & k\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_3\leftarrow R_3-(-3)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -1 & -6 \\ 0 & 3 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & k - 18\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_2\leftarrow \left(\frac{1}{3}\right)R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -1 & -6 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & k - 18\end{array}\right]
$$

The last row represents $0x_1+0x_2=k - 18$. Consistency therefore requires

$$
\begin{aligned}0 &=k - 18 \\ k &=18.\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot equations give $x_2=3$ and $x_1=-3$. These values also establish sufficiency:

$$
(-3)\mathbf{a}_1+(3)\mathbf{a}_2=\begin{bmatrix}6 \\ 18 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Therefore, $k=18$ is the only value for which the vector lies in the span.

knowledge_point.title: Finding the Value of an Unknown Such That a Vector Lies in the Span of Given Vectors

question.:question/problem:
Find the value of $k$ such that $\mathbf{b}\in\operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2\}$, where

$$
\mathbf{a}_1=\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\qquad\mathbf{a}_2=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\qquad\mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix}-4 \\ -12 \\ k\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
By definition, $\mathbf{b}\in\operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2\}$ exactly when $x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2=\mathbf{b}$ has a solution. Equating coordinates gives

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}- 3 x_{1} + 2 x_{2} &=-4 \\ - x_{1} - 2 x_{2} &=-12 \\ x_{1} + 2 x_{2} &=k\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Form the augmented matrix:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-3 & 2 & -4 \\ -1 & -2 & -12 \\ 1 & 2 & k\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_1\leftarrow \left(- \frac{1}{3}\right)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & - \frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ -1 & -2 & -12 \\ 1 & 2 & k\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_2\leftarrow R_2-(-1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & - \frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 0 & - \frac{8}{3} & - \frac{32}{3} \\ 1 & 2 & k\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_3\leftarrow R_3-(1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & - \frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 0 & - \frac{8}{3} & - \frac{32}{3} \\ 0 & \frac{8}{3} & k - \frac{4}{3}\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_2\leftarrow \left(- \frac{3}{8}\right)R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & - \frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & \frac{8}{3} & k - \frac{4}{3}\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_3\leftarrow R_3-\left(\frac{8}{3}\right)R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & - \frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & k - 12\end{array}\right]
$$

The last row represents $0x_1+0x_2=k - 12$. Consistency therefore requires

$$
\begin{aligned}0 &=k - 12 \\ k &=12.\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot equations give $x_2=4$ and $x_1=4$. These values also establish sufficiency:

$$
(4)\mathbf{a}_1+(4)\mathbf{a}_2=\begin{bmatrix}-4 \\ -12 \\ 12\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Therefore, $k=12$ is the only value for which the vector lies in the span.
